Kara-Zor-El, also known as Supergirl and Linda Lang, is a Kryptonian superhero based in Metropolis. Kara is Superman's cousin, Lana Lang's adopted niece, and a member of the Justice League, the Legion of Super-Heroes, and the Supermans of America.

Kryton Survivor
Kara Zor-El is the daughter of Zor-El and Alura In-Ze, Superman's uncles on her father's side. Kara is actually fifteen years older than her cousin Kal-El (Superman). Kara and her parents lived in the city of Argo when the villain Brainiac attacked Krypton and took the city of Kandor. Zor-El managed to reproduce Brainiac's technology and create a force field surrounding Argo. Said field saved the Argoans when Krypton exploded. Unfortunately, Brainiac later attacked Argo, and Kara's parents had to put her on a ship scheduled to travel to Earth. Kara's ship became trapped in a Kryptonite meteor, and the ship's life support systems put her into suspended animation, stopping her from aging. Kara arrived thirty years after her cousin.

Superman/Batman: Supergirl of Kryton
Kara's rocket landed in Gotham Bay, where she was found by Superman and Batman. Superman was excited to find someone from her family and wanted to take her to live with him and Lois, but Batman was suspicious of the girl, and Wonder Woman decided to take her to Paradise Island and train her. During her stay, Darkseid attacked the island, and her troops kidnapped her and brainwashed her into serving him. Kara was rescued by Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman and Big Barda, and subsequently adopted under the name "Supergirl".


But even though Kara took on this new role, she felt like she didn't quite fit in on Earth or with other heroes.

While she was trying to find her place on her new planet Lex Luthor attacked her. Luthor easily defeated Supergirl, exposing her to a piece of Black Kryptonia. The Kryptonite chunk created an evil double of Kara who called herself "Dark Supergirl."

That double pretended that Zor-El sent his daughter to Earth to kill baby Kal-El. Supergirl refused to believe her story, and the two fought.

Their battle - which involved the League - ended when Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman arrived to stop them. Supergirl then asked Wonder Woman to bind them with her Lasso of Truth and ask "Who is Kara Zor-El?"

Both Supergirls merged and "Dark Supergirl" disappeared in the process. Kara decided that although she still did not recover her memories, her past was not important, and her cousin, Bruce and Diana were now her parental figures.


Shortly after, the Infinite Crisis broke out. Kara joined Donna Troy's team and during a battle in space, she was hit by a modified Zeta Beam and disappeared.

Kara reappeared in the 31st century, where she was revered as one of the heroes of Superman's family, and she encountered the Legion of Super-Heroes. She came to the conclusion that she was dreaming and none of it was real. Saturn Girl, trying to learn how Kara came to be in her time, explored Kara's mind and found one particularly vivid memory: the Zeta Ray accident.

Cosmic Boy theorized that Kara had convinced himself that her life was a dream to rationalize her fantastical existence. In a relatively short period of time (due to suspended animation) she lost her planet, her parents, arrived on another planet and found that her cousin was an adult and a hero instead of a baby, acquired extraordinary powers, became to be a "living legend" and was found a thousand years in the future without explanation.

Cosmic Boy had to resort to somewhat rough methods to help her accept reality. Kara lived several adventures with the Legion, fighting in the War with the Dominators and being elected leader of the team until Brainiac 5 managed to create a machine that could send her to the past.

Kara returned a year and a month after the "Infinite Crisis" and during "World War III". Upon her arrival she found that Superboy had died in combat and Superman had lost his powers. Kara began to feel alone and isolated, but she dedicated herself to protecting Metropolis along with the heroes Booster Gold and Supernova.

Supergirl and Power Girl created the identities of Flamebird and Nightwing to fight crime in the city of Kandor and overthrow a cult led by the villains Ultraman and Saturn Queen.


After returning from Candor, Kara sold Batman Kryptonian technology to gain financial independence and buy her own apartment. She also strengthened her relationship with the Kent Family and found that she had several things in common with Cassie Sandsmark. Cassie was Conner Kent's girlfriend -Superboy- and she missed him too. While comforting each other, both girls became friends.

However, Kara was unknowingly suffering from poisoning caused by her continued exposure to Kryptonite. This affliction was the root of her amnesia and caused continuous mood and personality changes, lack of concentration, and horrible hallucinations in which her father was a monster who wanted to kill her cousin and experimented on her. Kara didn't want to believe it at first, but after a battle against Cassandra Cain in which crystals erupted from her body (another effect of poisoning: her blood crystallized upon contact with oxygen), Kara began to wonder if her hallucinations weren't real. .

Meanwhile, Kara collaborated with Green Lantern Hal Jordan on a mission to the casino world of Ventura. Kara was acting strangely flirtatious and playful with Hal. After the mission Kara revealed that she had behaved that way in reaction to Hal's own comments, and to attract the criminals they were looking for.

Upon returning to the planet, Kara's hallucinations worsened. She not only saw her father killing people and some kind of ghosts emerging from the Ghost Zone, but she also saw the Earth and her friends being possessed by those ghosts.

She soon discovered that these events were nothing more than hallucinations and visions, the work of an entity called the Dark Angel, a servant of the Monitors charged with identifying and destroying anomalies that threaten the Multiverse. Dark Angel had become convinced that Kara was one of those anomalies and put her through a test to prove it. Kara passed her tests, and one of the Monitors appeared to apologize for her employee's actions.

Now free, Kara decided to return to Earth and apologize to all the people she had hurt with her behavior for a year. Kara apologized to her cousin, and Clark hugged her. After repairing their relationship, both cousins raced to the Fortress of Solitude.


Shortly after, Supergirl and Wonder Girl (Cassie Sandsmark) hear that the Amazons have invaded Washington, DC, and because of the McCarran Homeland Security Act passed by the president, women are being locked up in concentration camps. Including Alison Sandsmark, Wonder Girl's mother. Supergirl and Wonder Girl attack the field to free them, but the Teen Titans appear to try to stop them, and Robin (Tim Drake) insists that they need to find a better solution to the conflict.

Kara and Cassie decide to fly to Washington and speak to Queen Hippolyta. The queen of the Amazons told them that there could be no negotiation without a face to face with the president of the United States, and convinced them to bring him to her. Kara and Cassie stormed the president's plane, and then they realized they had done something very stupid. Kara then did her best to make amends for her mistake.

Kara joined the Teen Titans shortly after. Her time as a Titan was very brief, but she continued to participate in several adventures of the young heroes.


Kara met two travelers from the future, Val Armor -Karate Kid- and Luornu Dungo -Triplicate Girl-, two members of the Legion of Super-Heroes, but not from the timeline she had visited.

Supergirl assisted them in combating a cyborg named Equus, and during that battle she recovered her memories from the 31st century that had been erased before her return.


Supergirl then helped Superman and the Green Lantern find out the origins of an invading alien army. Kara attempted to locate them, but a solar flare distracted her, making it impossible to find her point of origin. Kara felt like a failure, but Superman congratulated her for trying to do the best she could.

Later Supergirl encountered what would become one of her worst enemies, Reactron. Reactron - who claimed to have the power of a star in his suit - attempted to destroy Metropolis with a wave of nuclear energy. Supergirl fought him twice. The first time she lost, but the second time she realized that the source of her power was a metallic circle placed on her chest. Supergirl ripped off said circle and defeated him.

During the Reactron attack Kara found an eleven year old boy named Thomas Price who was dying of cancer. Supergirl vowed to save her life, even though Superman and other heroes warned her that her powers are useless against that kind of thing.

Kara was determined to save him, however, and tried everything, but although she found a possible cure, it was too late. Thomas was already dead.

Right after, while trying to recover from the disappointment, Kara teamed up with a former member of the Young Justice super-team, Empress, to save her parents from a man named Eddie Rose. Rose was almost killed during the battle between Doomsday and Superman, but lost the use of his legs and became cynical and bitter. He wanted to turn the people against the superheroes, so he kidnapped Empress's family to force them to lead Supergirl into a trap. However, Supergirl managed to stop Rose and rescue Empress's parents.


A streak of mistakes and errors in judgment, coupled with an article written by a Daily Planet columnist named Cat Grant titled "Why the World Doesn't Need Supergirl", led Kara to question her worth and competence. Clark Kent suggested to her cousin that she create a secret identity to relax and not end up burned out by trying to be a superhero 24 hours a day.

Supergirl's powers are almost completely similar to those of her cousin: Super strength, super speed (able to match the speed of light), flight, almost total invulnerability (able to easily withstand the explosion of 11 solar systems), super hearing, telescopic vision and microscopic, x-ray vision, frozen breath, heat vision (capable of launching heat rays as hot as the sun), infra red vision, magnetic spectrum vision weakness Green Kryptonite It is the most common of all. In Kryptonians with superpowers, it causes immediate loss of power, weakness and physical pain, and can kill in just a few hours. The effects were described in a variety of ways, from loss only during the exposure time, to total loss for a few minutes even after exposure. She was originally shown to be harmless to humans and non-powered Kryptonians.

personality
brave, compassionate and determined. Kara is often shown as a heroic young woman with a strong sense of duty and responsibility, especially when it comes to protecting the innocent and fighting evil.

Although she can sometimes be impulsive and have difficulty controlling her temper, she has also been portrayed as loving, friendly, and willing to help others.

hero costume
Top: Their costume usually consists of a tight-fitting, sleeveless top that covers the shoulders and torso. The upper often features the iconic House of El logo, similar to Superman's but with a stylized "S" inside a pentagon-shaped shield.

High collar or V-neckline: Depending on the version, the suit may have a high collar that completely covers the neck and upper chest, or a more open V-neckline.

Belt: Often wears a yellow or gold belt around the waist, which can be thin or wider depending on the design.

Skirt or pants: The bottom of the suit may consist of a short skirt or tight pants, often colored dark blue or red to match the rest of the suit.

Boots: Supergirl usually wears tall boots that reach to the bottom of her knees. These boots are usually red and sometimes have yellow details.

Cape: In some versions, Supergirl wears a short cape that hangs from her shoulders, usually the same color as the rest of the costume.

I don't need Supergirl. I still couldn't believe people thought that about me. I always tried to do the right thing because it feels like the first time I came to earth alone. Clark told me I should look up my secret identity but it was difficult. How can I be a hero when people think that about me? I know I have made mistakes but I have always tried to help people. Maybe I'm exaggerating a little but I can't help but feel that way. I decided to fly a little to think, I went to several places to think, after a while I went home*

*Clark paid me for an apartment, where I lived for 6 months in metropolis.
